chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then he proved himself false (in his accusation). Is his child returned to him? He said: If he proved himself false, he is given the flogging (for li'an) and his child is returned to him, and his wife is not returned to him forever.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an if the husband's accusation is proven false?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a husband who falsely completes the li'an procedure is subject to the hadd punishment for qadhf (false accusation) and loses the right to remarry his wife, yet the child remains his. This highlights the Shia juristic view that li'an creates a permanent bond of 'permanent divorce' (talaq ba'in) rather than a revocable one, emphasizing the finality of the oath's legal weight even if the accusation is later disproven.
